title: Archive and Orbit Again
premise: Coral Quintana is a clone of the murdered detective whose unsolved case he inherited — and the only person both warring fleets believe can arbitrate their fragile truce, because each thinks he's someone else entirely. When the colony's children begin dreaming a shared dream of a buried ship beneath the ice, Coral discovers the dream is a distress signal from the original's killer, still alive and hiding in the wreck. To keep two fleets from annihilating each other over the salvage, Coral must maintain his double identity while following the dream's clues to the truth of his own murder. In the end, Coral exposes the killer, chooses love and colony over fleet duty, and lets both identities die so a new one — his own — can finally begin.
about_author: Wren Vasquez is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who wrote her first novel during long shifts monitoring contested shipping lanes. She lives in a coastal town where she collects tide charts and insists every story needs at least one stubborn cargo hauler.

chapters.title: Deadweight
chapters.summary: Coral Quintana's POV. Hauling contraband seed crates through a blockade checkpoint, Coral flashes his dead original's credentials to slip past a patrol — a lie that works too well. Emotional beat: weary competence masking the hollow of living as a copy.

chapters.title: The Children's Hour
chapters.summary: Schoolteacher Imani Okafor's POV. Twenty-three children fall asleep simultaneously in class and wake reciting identical words about ice and a door. Imani reports it to the joint garrison, unknowingly summoning both fleets' attention. Beat: creeping dread wrapped in tenderness.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Badge
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Summoned by Fleet Arbiter Sorel, who calls him 'Detective Quintana,' Coral realizes the truce depends on him being the man he was cloned from. He accepts the investigation into the shared dream rather than reveal himself. Beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ice Under the Skin
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani maps the children's dream fragments onto the colony's old survey charts and finds they point to a crater never officially explored. She hesitates to tell Coral, distrusting anyone wearing a fleet badge. Beat: quiet defiance.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Digging into his original's cold case files for context, Coral finds the murder weapon matched nothing on record — but matches a hull alloy used by neither fleet. Someone third was here all along. Beat: the thrill of a real clue.

chapters.title: The Truce Table
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral/Imani POV. At a tense joint session, both fleets demand the dream be declared enemy psychological warfare. Coral stalls by proposing a civilian survey expedition, buying time and volunteering himself. Beat: diplomacy as knife-edge performance.

chapters.title: What the Body Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the glacier approach, Coral experiences muscle memory that isn't his — the original climbed this ice before dying. The clone body remembers the route to the crater. Beat: grief for a life he inherited like debt.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. Imani decodes the children's recurring phrase as coordinates plus a countdown — eleven days. When she transmits this to Coral, an unknown party intercepts the message. Beat: the moment privacy dies and stakes go public.

chapters.title: The Door in the Dream
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The expedition reaches the crater and finds a half-buried ship older than either fleet's charter. Inside, a live power source pulses in rhythm with the children's sleep cycles. Beat: awe curdling into violation.

chapters.title: Brother, Interrupted
chapters.summary: New character POV: Ede Quintana, Coral's fellow clone raised by the original's family, arrives claiming fleet authority and family grief. Ede wants the case closed quietly — and Coral gone. Beat: jealousy dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral and Ede clash over how to handle the countdown; Ede reveals the fleets have secretly agreed to scuttle the ship with the crater — and everyone who knows about it. Beat: betrayal reframing allies as targets.

chapters.title: Salt and Starlight
chapters.summary: Coral and Imani dual POV. Sheltering from a storm, Coral tells Imani the truth about being a clone; she admits she already knew and stayed anyway. First kiss against the wind. Beat: belonging chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: The Killer's Lullaby
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Following the dream's final fragment, Coral finds a hidden module in the wreck — occupied. The original's killer, Dr. Halloway, has been broadcasting the dream to keep someone coming to free him. Beat: horror meeting pity.

chapters.title: Confession in Cryo
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Dying in a failing cryo-stasis, Halloway confesses: he killed the original because the detective discovered the ship is a generation vessel carrying sleeping colonists — people both fleets would harvest or destroy. Beat: monstrous logic almost making sense.

chapters.title: Harvest Terms
chapters.summary: Sorel's POV. The arbiter learns what's in the ship and orders immediate seizure, truce be damned. Coral is ordered to stand down and hand over Halloway's evidence. Beat: duty revealed as appetite.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral fabricates evidence that the ship is a plague vault, forcing both fleets to quarantine rather than board — the lie that holds them apart. It costs him Sorel's trust and Ede's silence. Beat: moral weight of necessary deception.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. The children's dream ends abruptly; the ship's systems begin waking the sleepers early. With fleets massing overhead, Imani and Coral have hours, not days. Beat: breathless acceleration.

chapters.title: Ede's Choice
chapters.summary: Ede's POV. Ordered to kill Coral and stage an accident, Ede instead confronts him in the wreck — and chooses brotherhood over orders, feeding the fleets false telemetry. Beat: redemption bought at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Archive and Orbit
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax: Coral broadcasts Halloway's full confession and the sleepers' living faces to both fleets and the colony at once, betting everything that ordinary people will refuse the harvest. Fleets stall; crowds gather. Beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: The Long Wake
chapters.summary: Imani's POV. The first sleepers wake to Imani's classroom full of children who dreamed them into safety. Negotiations begin under colony, not fleet, authority. Beat: exhausted, hard-won hope.

chapters.title: Two Funerals and a Name
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral publicly retires both identities — the detective and the clone — burying the original's badge and his own forged papers. Sorel resigns; Ede departs to testify. Beat: mourning as liberation.

chapters.title: Again
chapters.summary: Coral and Imani dual POV. Months later, Coral pilots a reflagged colony ship hauling the awakened colonists to new orbits, Imani beside him, the children waving from the dock. He signs the log with a name no one gave him. Beat: arrival — belonging, identity, and love, all chosen.
